chapter_seo_title: RMJI Ch. 353: The Sky Fire Descends - A Brutal Counter-Ambush
chapter_meta_description: Elder Huang’s ambush fails as a mid-grade Heavenly Fire spell rains down on Yellow Maple Valley. Surrounded by the Six Demonic Sects and two Core Formation foes, a desperate breakout begins.
og_title: A Scorching Sky & A Broken Trap
og_description: The hunters become the hunted as a massive Heavenly Fire spell turns the sky to magma, forcing a desperate last stand against two legendary Core Formation cultivators.
twitter_title: When the Sky Turns to Magma
twitter_description: Elder Huang’s perfect ambush is destroyed by a mid-grade spell. Now, Yellow Maple Valley must face the Six Demonic Sects alone.

lore_anchors.definition: A high-grade magic treasure that generates a concealing cloud of mist capable of hiding an entire group, used here by Elder Huang for a failed ambush. It is a powerful, specialized tool for covert movement and tactical positioning, not used for direct combat.

A mid-to-advanced grade fire spell that transforms the sky into a churning, molten cloud of magma, raining down destructive droplets for a sustained period. It represents a qualitative shift in power from lower-grade spells, serving as an area-denial and mana-exhaustion weapon.

The infamous nickname for a pair of Core Formation cultivators from the Six Demonic Sects. The woman is seductively beautiful and deadly, while her partner is a skeletal, terrifying figure. Their appearance signals a deadly escalation in the conflict.

The third major cultivation realm, representing a massive power increase over Foundation Establishment. A Core Formation cultivator's senses and combat capabilities are on an entirely different level, allowing them to detect an entire battlefield and command the course of a battle against lower-tier enemies.

The second major realm of cultivation. Foundation Establishment cultivators are the 'junior officers' of a sect, possessing enough power to fight effectively but still utterly inferior to a single Core Formation master. In this battle, they are described as being drained of mana by the Heavenly Fire Technique.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn't Elder Huang just escape the spell range?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He explains it explicitly: the spell is already fully formed and has a wide area of effect. Running would take them out of the frying pan and into the fire, likely isolating them and making them easier targets for the enemy closing in. The only option was to use their combined power to endure the bombardment.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who are the 'Red Powder and White Skeleton'?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are a legendary duo of Core Formation cultivators from the Six Demonic Sects. The woman (Red Powder/Beauty) is seductive and deadly, while the man (White Skeleton) is a horrifying, skeletal figure. Their reputation alone is enough to demoralize an entire expedition.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li give his sword to Qu Hun?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It's a purely practical, cost-benefit calculation. Han Li has no use for a greatsword in a large-scale aerial battle; he prefers a more discreet flying blade. Qu Hun is a soulless, strong puppet, so giving him the greatsword turns a useless item into a potential combat asset with no extra risk to Han Li.
